title: Chain Controls opens its own second WebSocket on every visit and never really closes it: the cleanup closes the socket, but the close handler then arms a new 3 s reconnect that nothing cancels, so each visit leaves a socket that reconnects (and reloads positions, chains and pause state) for as long as the tab is open

evidence.note: const { chainStatuses } = useWebSocket(): a second connection next to the shared provider
the shared provider every other page reads through useWs()
cleanup: clear the pending timer, then wsRef.current.close()
onclose (which runs after close() completes, i.e. after the cleanup) sets wsRef.current = null and arms setTimeout(connect, 3000)
connect() then finds wsRef.current null and opens a new socket, whose own onclose re-arms again; nothing references this hook instance any more
the 5 s live-quote broadcast runs while any authenticated socket is connected (AUD-API-012)

sibling_sites_checked: Every caller of useWebSocket: WebSocketContext.tsx:33 (the shared provider) and ChainControls.tsx:21 (this finding). The same cleanup defect exists in the shared provider; it matters only if the provider unmounts. App.tsx:11-40 and :48-87 mount a WebSocketProvider inside each route's own AuthGuard; whether React Router reuses that instance across route changes was not established without running the app (no browser run in Phase 22), so a leak per navigation is recorded as possible, not proven. Other timers in the dashboard: GapDetectedBanner none; AntiRugExitDetailModal 2 s copy toast (harmless); PnLChart resize listener removed on unmount.
severity_rationale: S3: resource leak and ops friction. Each visit adds a permanent reconnecting client: more authenticated sockets receiving every broadcast, three extra API reads per reconnect, and the server's 5 s quote loop kept running. Over a long session this adds RPC and CPU load on the bot process that also runs the exits (AUD-API-012). No direct money effect.
recommendation: Read chain statuses from the shared useWs() context instead of a second hook; in the hook, set a "closed by cleanup" flag (or remove onclose) before close() so the cleanup cannot re-arm the reconnect. Phase 29.
